papers.title: Direct Detection of Solar Neutrinos to Probe Tensions and Break Degeneracies in Long-Baseline Neutrino Experiments
papers.abstract: Long-baseline (LBL) accelerator experiments are sensitive not only to the standard neutrino oscillation parameters but also to new physics. Currently, there exists a tension between NOvA and T2K data that can be explained by vector non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI) with complex couplings, which in turn introduce degeneracies in LBL measurements. We demonstrate that dark matter direct detection experiments can use their measurements of solar neutrinos to test the NSI resolution of this tension and to break these degeneracies. Using recent solar neutrino data from LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T, we show that dark matter direct detection experiments already constrain part of the NSI solution of the NOvA-T2K tension. These experiments can also probe parts of the NSI parameter space that even DUNE will be blind to. Our analysis combines nuclear recoils from $^8$B neutrinos and electron recoils from $pp$ neutrinos. A future xenon experiment, such as XLZD or PandaX-xT, will be able to cover a significant fraction of the NSI solution of the NOvA-T2K tension.
papers.reason: Directly tackles vector non-standard neutrino interactions resolving NOvA-T2K tensions using solar neutrino data from LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T, squarely in core low-energy neutrino phenomenology.

summary.tldr: Solar neutrino CEvNS and electron scattering in dark matter direct detection experiments can break parameter degeneracies in long-baseline neutrino experiments and constrain non-standard neutrino interaction solutions to the NOvA-T2K tension.
summary.novel_idea: The authors connect solar neutrino measurements at dark matter direct detection (DM-DD) facilities directly to long-baseline (LBL) accelerator anomalies. They show that combining nuclear recoils (CEvNS from $^8$B) and electron recoils (E$\nu$ES from $pp$) breaks diagonal parameter degeneracies (such as $\mathcal{E}_{ee} - \mathcal{E}_{\mu\mu}$) that even DUNE cannot resolve on its own.
summary.method: The authors compute differential event rates using generalized CEvNS and E$\nu$ES cross sections that preserve neutrino flavor density-matrix coherences from propagation to detection. They build a profile log-likelihood incorporating experimental and solar flux nuisance parameters using existing data from LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T, alongside sensitivity projections for next-generation observatories (XLZD, PandaX-xT).
key_results: Current LZ and XENONnT nuclear recoil data already rule out portions of the complex NSI parameter space ($|\mathcal{E}_{e\tau}| \sim 0.2$, $\phi_{e\tau} \sim 3\pi/2$) preferred as a solution to the NOvA-T2K $\delta_{\text{CP}}$ tension.

A future multi-ton xenon detector (such as XLZD) with a $1\text{ keV}_{\text{nr}}$ threshold can probe almost the entire $1\sigma$ preferred NOvA-T2K tension region for $\mathcal{E}_{e\tau}$ and a significant fraction for $\mathcal{E}_{e\mu}$.

Profiling over absolute diagonal NSI parameters demonstrates that DM-DD solar scattering breaks the blind diagonal LBL degeneracy in $(|\mathcal{E}_{e\tau}|, \mathcal{E}_{ee} - \mathcal{E}_{\mu\mu})$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to your work on BSM neutrino interactions, CEvNS phenomenology, and oscillation analysis systematics. It provides an external handle from low-energy scattering to break degeneracies in DUNE and Hyper-K matter-effect fits.
summary.caveats: Assumes a contact dimension-6 vector operator framework, requiring mediator masses above $\sim 10\text{ MeV}$ to remain consistent with BBN while avoiding momentum-transfer dependence in CEvNS; relies on standard solar model flux uncertainties (6-12%).

papers.title: Excited-State Effects in Nucleon Sigma Terms from a Variational Analysis
papers.abstract: We investigate excited-state effects in nucleon sigma-terms in lattice QCD using twisted-mass clover-improved fermion ensembles. We study correlation functions with nucleon and multihadron nucleon-$\sigma$-meson interpolating operators. The analysis is performed using three gauge ensembles, including one ensemble simulated with two degenerate light, a strange, and a charm quark with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical value. We solve the generalized eigenvalue problem that arises from the matrix of correlators and show that the three-point function for the light sigma-term obtained using the optimal linear combination of interpolating operators has substantially reduced time dependence without loss of statistical precision. We apply Laplace filtering and investigate residual excited-state contributions in the extraction of $\sigma_{\pi N}$. Using the same optimal linear combination of correlators as for $\sigma_{\pi N}$ for the strange sigma-term we also observe suppressed excited state contributions over an extended range of source--sink time separations. For the charm sigma-term, we observe negligible time dependence within the large statistical uncertainties, and these improvements show no significant effect.
papers.topic: Excited-state effects in nucleon sigma terms
papers.reason: Performs a lattice QCD variational analysis using optimal multi-hadron operators to suppress excited-state contamination in nucleon light- and strange-sigma terms.

summary.tldr: A variational GEVP analysis with multihadron $N\sigma$ interpolators and Laplace filtering suppresses excited-state contamination in lattice QCD extractions of nucleon scalar sigma-terms at physical pion masses.
summary.novel_idea: The study demonstrates the implementation of an enlarged interpolator basis combining standard nucleon and multihadron $N\sigma$-meson operators at physical pion masses in $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass lattice QCD. It pairs this variational (GEVP) setup with time-slice Laplace filtering to directly probe and control multihadron contamination in nucleon scalar matrix elements.
summary.method: Simulations use twisted-mass clover-improved fermions at maximal twist on three gauge ensembles, prominently the physical-point ensemble cB211.072.64 ($m_\pi \approx 139\text{ MeV}$, $a \approx 0.08\text{ fm}$). A $2\times 2$ GEVP is solved to construct an optimal GEVP-improved nucleon operator, and three-point correlation functions are analyzed using multi-state spectral fits and localized Laplace filtering.
key_results: For the light-quark sigma term on the physical ensemble, the analysis yields $\sigma_{\pi N} = 45.7(3.0)_{\text{stat}}(3.3)_{\text{syst}}\text{ MeV}$, favoring the lower range of existing lattice extractions over Roy-Steiner pionic-atom determinations ($55.9 \pm 3.5\text{ MeV}$).

GEVP improvement significantly flattens the source-sink and insertion time dependence of the strange sigma term three-point ratio, resulting in $\sigma_s = 42.1(6.5)_{\text{stat}}(2.3)_{\text{syst}}\text{ MeV}$.
The charm sigma term shows mild excited-state sensitivity, yielding $\sigma_c = 107.4(30.4)_{\text{stat}}(0.6)_{\text{syst}}\text{ MeV}$, consistent with the heavy-quark expansion.
summary.why_it_matters: Highly relevant to lattice QCD methodology for hadron structure. The techniques developed here to control low-lying multihadron excited states ($N\pi, N\pi\pi, N\sigma$) directly transfer to reducing systematics in nucleon axial and vector form factor calculations needed for neutrino-nucleus event generators.
summary.caveats: Despite GEVP improvement, Laplace filtering reveals residual excited-state contamination in $\sigma_{\pi N}$, indicating that a larger operator basis (including explicit $N\pi$ or $N\pi\pi$ interpolators) will be required to resolve the tension with phenomenological extractions.

papers.title: Coherent states of neutrinos in rotating matter
papers.abstract: We study coherent states of neutrinos electroweakly interacting with rotating matter. We start with the Dirac equation for a massive neutrino propagating in background matter with a coordinate dependent effective potential. Then, we consider the limit of massless particles and the specific matter velocity profile. It allows us to reduce the neutrino Hamiltonian to the harmonic oscillator form. We find the exact solutions of the Dirac equation and construct the creation and annihilation operators. Using these results, we build the generalized coherent states of neutrinos. We provide the interpretation of these coherent states in terms of the classical physics. In particular, we demonstrate that the coherent states constructed approach plane waves in the limit of slow matter rotation. We also define the effective neutrino mass owing to the interaction of a massless neutrino with rotating matter. Then, we consider a special case of the generalized coherent states which are called the neutrino coherent states. The situation of the degenerate parameters of the system is also studied. Finally, we apply our results for astrophysical neutrinos propagating in dense matter of a rapidly rotating neutron star (NS). We calculate the effective neutrino masses for different neutrino energies for realistic parameters of NS.
papers.reason: Derives exact solutions of the Dirac equation and coherent states for neutrinos propagating through rotating matter, highly relevant to core low-energy and astrophysical neutrino contexts.

summary.tldr: Generalized coherent states for massless Dirac neutrinos electroweakly interacting with rotating matter are constructed in light-cone variables, yielding an effective mass and a smooth transition to plane waves.
summary.novel_idea: Stationary solutions of the Dirac equation for neutrinos in rotating matter do not smoothly reduce to plane waves as the angular velocity vanishes. The authors solve this by using light-cone coordinates and building generalized coherent states that diagonalize non-stationary integrals of motion, ensuring continuous transitions to free-particle plane waves.
summary.method: The Dirac equation with a coordinate-dependent axial-vector potential representing forward scattering in a uniformly rotating medium ($v = \Omega \times r$) is projected onto light-cone null hyperplanes ($u^0 = x^-$). For massless Dirac neutrinos, the transverse Hamiltonian maps onto a quantum harmonic oscillator, allowing the algebraic construction of coherent states via Bogoliubov transformations, followed by application to dense neutron star matter.
key_results: Constructed exact algebraic annihilation and creation operators acting directly on bispinor space for active neutrinos in rotating matter.

Demonstrated that the expectation values of neutrino position and momentum satisfy Ehrenfest relations matching a classical particle in a uniform magnetic field with cyclotron frequency $\omega_c = -s\Omega G_N / (\sqrt{2}(\lambda - G_N))$.

Calculated that electroweak interactions with rotating dense neutron star matter ($n_n \sim 10^{38}\text{ cm}^{-3}, \Omega \sim 10^3\text{ s}^{-1}$) induce an effective neutrino mass $m_{\text{eff}}$ on the order of a few $\text{eV}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Only tangentially relevant to core neutrino phenomenology. While it treats neutrino propagation in astrophysical environments (neutron stars), the mathematical formalisms are largely detached from neutrino-nucleus cross sections or oscillation experiment pipelines.
summary.caveats: Strictly relies on massless neutrinos to decouple the chiral projections in light-cone variables, and assumes an idealized infinite planar velocity profile that must be restricted geometrically to avoid superluminal rotation speeds.

papers.title: Universal enhancement of the pairing gap in a dilute Fermi superfluid
papers.abstract: At zero temperature, a dilute Fermi gas with an attractive contact interaction forms a superfluid with gapped fermionic excitations. We show that the gap at weak coupling can be organized as a trans-series expansion in the interaction strength and the asymptotic Gor'kov-Melik-Barkhudarov gap. Low-energy virtual quasiparticles generate corrections that are linear in the gap with a leading coefficient nearly 25$\times$ larger than the other known coefficients. This substantially increases the gap at intermediate densities, highlighting that systematic corrections are crucial for quantitative predictions.
papers.topic: Universal pairing gap in dilute Fermi gas
papers.reason: Derives a trans-series expansion showing low-energy virtual quasiparticles substantially enhance the pairing gap in dilute Fermi superfluids, highly relevant to ab initio nuclear many-body methods.

summary.tldr: The pairing gap in a dilute Fermi superfluid exhibits a trans-series expansion where low-energy virtual quasiparticles generate a large linear-in-gap correction that enhances the gap beyond the Gor'kov-Melik-Barkhudarov prediction.
summary.novel_idea: The paper reveals that the weak-coupling expansion of the superfluid gap is fundamentally a trans-series in coupling $\lambda = k_F a / \pi$ and the asymptotic Gor'kov-Melik-Barkhudarov (GMB) gap $x_0$. It identifies an entirely new kinematic sector linear in the gap $\Delta$, arising from virtual soft quasiparticles with energies $E \sim \Delta$, possessing an anomalously large coefficient.
summary.method: Starting from the exact Goldstone-pole condition on the amputated pairing vertex via the matrix Bethe-Salpeter equation in Nambu-Gor'kov space, the authors systematically expand the gap equation in explicit powers of the contact interaction $g$ and the gap $\Delta$. Soft and hard momentum integrations are separated, evaluating loop integrals in closed analytic form via modified Bessel function moments and the PSLQ algorithm.
key_results: Analytically evaluated the leading linear-in-gap coefficient as $c_{2,1} = 24.323\ldots$, which is roughly $25\times$ larger than typical perturbative coefficients ($|c_{n,0}| \le 1$).

Corrected prior literature errors in the hard-region next-to-next-to-leading order coefficient, finding $c_{1,0} = \frac{1}{3}\ln 2 + \frac{3}{2}\ln^2 2 - \frac{\pi^2}{36} - \frac{7}{2}\zeta(3) + \frac{14}{\pi^2}\text{G} + \frac{28}{\pi^2}\text{Li}_3(1/2) \approx 0.811$.

Found that the linear-in-gap correction dominates over GMB for $|k_F a| \gtrsim 0.3$, significantly increasing the pairing gap and creating a $\sim 2\sigma$ tension with available Quantum Monte Carlo and cold-atom data around $|k_F a| \approx 1$.
summary.why_it_matters: Touches nuclear many-body theory relevant to neutron star crust pairing and neutron matter equations of state. However, it focuses on contact-interaction superfluids rather than nuclear-structure or neutrino-interaction physics.
summary.caveats: Uses a zero-range contact interaction without finite-range nuclear forces or tensor correlations; the trans-series expansion loses perturbative stability for $|k_F a| \sim 1$ where corrections exceed the leading gap.

papers.title: Measuring $V_{cb}$ at electron-proton colliders
papers.abstract: We study the prospects for an independent determination of $V_{cb}$ from bottom-tagged charged-current deep-inelastic scattering at future electron-proton colliders: the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh. The transition $e^- c \to \nu_e b$ probes $|V_{cb}|^2$ through a process with different theoretical and experimental uncertainties from semileptonic $B$ decays. We fit ratios of $b$-tagged charged-current event counts over flavour-inclusive ones in kinematic bins, including correlated parton-distribution and flavour-tag calibration uncertainties, and floating the other CKM parameters. With projected parton distributions and tagging performance motivated by existing studies, we find a potential relative sensitivity in $|V_{cb}|$ of about $0.8\%$ at the LHeC with $1\,\rm{ab}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity and $0.7\%$ at FCC-eh with $2\,\rm{ab}^{-1}$. The corresponding EIC sensitivity is instead at the level of $20 - 30 \%$, depending on the configuration. The LHeC could thus provide a high-energy determination competitive with low-energy ones, but with substantially different dominant systematic uncertainties, on the timescale of its proposed operation between the HL-LHC and FCC-ee. We identify precise flavour-tag calibration and control of the kinematic response as the main requirements for realising this potential sensitivity.
papers.reason: Studies charged-current deep-inelastic scattering at electron-proton colliders (EIC, LHeC, FCC-eh) to extract CKM parameters, highly relevant to lepton-nucleus scattering and DIS systematics.

summary.tldr: Bottom-tagged charged-current deep-inelastic scattering ($e^- c \to \nu_e b$) at future electron-proton colliders like the LHeC and FCC-eh can measure $|V_{cb}|$ with sub-percent precision, independent of semileptonic $B$ decays.
summary.novel_idea: The author proposes an independent, high-energy determination of $|V_{cb}|$ using bottom-tagged charged-current (CC) deep-inelastic scattering ($e^- c \to \nu_e b$) at $ep$ colliders. Measuring ratios of $b$-tagged to inclusive CC DIS events in kinematic bins allows extraction of $|V_{cb}|$ free from the longstanding experimental and theoretical tensions between inclusive and exclusive semileptonic $B$ decays.
summary.method: The sensitivity is evaluated via a profiled Fisher information analysis using Born-level massive DIS kinematics ($m_b = 4.75\text{ GeV}$). The fit floats all other CKM elements, projected proton PDFs (NNPDF3.1 for EIC, PDF4LHC15_nnlo_lhec for LHeC/FCC-eh), single-top backgrounds modeled with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, and experimental tagging/mistag efficiency calibrations and shape distortions.
key_results: The LHeC with $1\text{ ab}^{-1}$ can achieve an expected relative precision on $|V_{cb}|$ of $0.79\%$ with polarized electrons ($P_e = -0.8$) and $0.89\%$ unpolarized.
FCC-eh ($2\text{ ab}^{-1}, P_e = -0.8$) achieves $0.67\%$ precision, whereas the EIC is statistically limited to a $20-30\%$ determination.
Reaching sub-percent precision at the LHeC requires calibrating the $b$-tagging efficiency to $\sim 1\%$ and controlling mistag kinematic shape variations across $y$ to within a few percent.

Backgrounds from neutral-current DIS with a lost electron are shown to impact $|V_{cb}|$ precision by $\le 1\%$ at the LHeC provided the electron loss probability is $p_{\text{loss}} \lesssim 10^{-3}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly intersects your interest in lepton-hadron scattering, CC DIS kinematics, and charm/bottom PDF inputs. High-energy CC DIS modeling and tagging calibration techniques map directly onto high-energy neutrino scattering physics (such as at FASER$\nu$, the Forward Physics Facility, or a muon collider neutrino program).
summary.caveats: The calculation relies on Born-level matrix elements without higher-order QCD/electroweak radiative corrections or detector-level hadronization/smearing simulations.

papers.title: Pythia-Contrib: a modular contribution framework for the Pythia 8 event generator
papers.abstract: Pythia is a general-purpose Monte Carlo event generator used in particle, astroparticle, and nuclear physics, by theorists and experimentalists, to simulate particle collisions. Because of the size and diversity of the user community, it is challenging to address all of the needs for new and varied physics models. This paper describes the Pythia-Contrib system, which allows for third-party developers to contribute code to Pythia without introducing external software dependencies to the Pythia code base.
papers.reason: Introduces Pythia-Contrib, a modular framework for the Pythia 8 event generator, which is directly relevant to neutrino event generator development and Monte Carlo physics simulations.

summary.tldr: Introduces Pythia-Contrib, a modular runtime plugin framework allowing third-party developers to contribute new models and external dependencies to Pythia 8 without modifying or bloating the core codebase.
summary.novel_idea: Inspired by FastJet-Contrib, Pythia-Contrib creates an official repository and build harness for runtime-loadable Pythia 8 plugins. It isolates third-party code and arbitrary external library dependencies from the core distribution while preserving versioning, documentation standards, and individual author attribution.
summary.method: The framework utilizes C++ runtime polymorphism where contributors derive plugin classes from standard Pythia 8 base classes. Packages are compiled into standalone shared libraries and linked dynamically at execution via Pythia's existing plugin hooks. A centralized 'use' repository provides unified management and configuration tools.
key_results: Establishes a centralized plugin registry and installation management system hosted at gitlab.com/pythia8-contrib.
Demonstrates zero-dependency impact on the core Pythia 8.318 library when dynamically loading complex external user plugins at runtime.
Provides standardized packaging, licensing, and academic citation infrastructure for community contributions.
summary.why_it_matters: While primarily a high-energy software framework, this architecture could serve as a convenient deployment vehicle for specialized neutrino-induced hadronization models, shallow-inelastic fragmentation schemes, or high-energy neutrino BSM modules used in tools like GENIE or Achilles.
summary.caveats: Long-term reliability depends heavily on third-party package maintainers updating their shared plugins against major Pythia 8 API revisions.

papers.title: Constraining three-nucleon forces in nuclear lattice effective field theory
papers.abstract: We study short-range three-nucleon forces (3NFs) in nuclear lattice effective field theory with a chiral two-nucleon interaction at N${}^3$LO. The one-pion-exchange ($c_D$) and contact ($c_E$) terms of the leading 3NF are decomposed into locally and non-locally smeared components and supplemented by partial-wave-resolved pair contacts coupled to the density of a third nucleon. We determine their coefficients from nuclear binding energies for nuclei in the mass range from $A=3$ to $A=40$ and neutron--alpha finite-volume energies. This allows to work out the minimal three-nucleon force that can be used for future precision studies in NLEFT.
papers.reason: Constrains short-range three-nucleon forces in nuclear lattice effective field theory from light to medium nuclei, directly relevant to ab initio nuclear structure and neutrino-nucleus interactions.

summary.tldr: Constrains short-range chiral three-nucleon forces in nuclear lattice effective field theory at N3LO using nuclear binding energies up to $A=40$ and neutron-alpha scattering data.
summary.novel_idea: The authors construct a minimal short-range three-nucleon force (3NF) for Nuclear Lattice EFT by decomposing leading $c_D$ and $c_E$ terms into locally and nonlocally smeared components. They supplement these with partial-wave-resolved two-nucleon contact operators coupled to the scalar-isoscalar density of a third spectator nucleon, bypassing full three-body Jacobi partial-wave expansions.
summary.method: Calculations employ an N3LO two-nucleon chiral interaction and a fixed Roy-Steiner two-pion-exchange 3NF on the lattice. Matrix elements are evaluated in first-order perturbation theory via wave-function matching across six leading-order reference Hamiltonian variants. The low-energy constants for up to 40 candidate 3NF operators are fitted using stochastic optimization against 38 observables: $E/A$ for 26 nuclei ($A=3$ to $40$, including $^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}$, $^{36}\text{Ar}$, $^{40}\text{Ca}$) and finite-volume $n\text{--}\alpha$ levels.
key_results: Without short-range 3NFs, the relative binding-energy RMSD across the nuclear chart is $21.6\%$; fitting five 3NF terms reduces this RMSD to $2.22\%$ (and $2.15\%$ for six terms).
Finite-volume $n\text{--}\alpha$ scattering energies achieve RMSDs of $0.174\text{ MeV}$ ($^2P_{3/2}$) and $0.234\text{ MeV}$ ($^2P_{1/2}$) for the top-50 five-term ensemble.
All top-50 five-term fits select two extended Cartesian contact terms ($[c_E^{(0)}]_{044}$, $[c_E^{(0)}]_{222}$) alongside the partial-wave-resolved $^3P_1$ contact $D_{{}^3P_1}$.

Accurately reproduces ground-state binding energies for primary neutrino target nuclei, including $^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}$, $^{36}\text{Ar}$, and $^{40}\text{Ca}$, within $\sim 2\text{--}4\%$ relative deviations.
summary.why_it_matters: Constraining 3NFs up to $^{36}\text{Ar}$ and $^{40}\text{Ca}$ in chiral EFT is an essential step toward precision nuclear wave functions and spectral functions needed to model axial current matrix elements and 2p2h responses in DUNE and Hyper-K event generators.
summary.caveats: The reported uncertainties omit chiral EFT truncation and lattice-spacing extrapolation errors, and a persistent signed residual remains in the $n\text{--}\alpha$ $^2P_{1/2}$ finite-volume level.

papers.title: Correlation of galactic very-high-energy gamma-ray sources detected by LHAASO with high-energy neutrinos
papers.abstract: We conducted an investigation into the possible correlation between very-high-energy (VHE, $E>$ 0.1 TeV) gamma-ray sources, as identified by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO), and high-energy neutrino events captured by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. For this analysis, we utilized the First LHAASO catalog, which comprises 90 VHE gamma-ray sources, and the IceCube Event Catalog of Alert Tracks (IceCat-1), which includes 348 track-like neutrino events. Through Monte Carlo simulations, we assessed the correlations between the neutrino events and LHAASO sources, achieving the best p-values of 0.237, 0.312, and 0.115, respectively, for all LHAASO sources, KM2A sources, and WCDA sources. These findings imply that the spatial coincidence between LHAASO sources and neutrino alerts is relatively weak. Furthermore, under the assumption that gamma-rays are exclusively generated through hadronic interactions, we estimated the most optimistic theoretical neutrino fluxes from LHAASO sources and compared them with the IceCube observed fluxes. The results indicate that the majority of these sources are improbable counterparts to the detected neutrinos. In conclusion, LHAASO sources could be potential galactic neutrino emitters but currently do not exhibit compelling evidence, thereby underscoring the necessity for elevated sensitivity levels in forthcoming detection instruments like IceCube-Gen2.
papers.reason: Investigates spatial correlations between VHE LHAASO gamma-ray sources and IceCube high-energy neutrino events, assessing hadronic emission scenarios.

summary.tldr: Demonstrates that the spatial coincidence between 90 LHAASO very-high-energy gamma-ray sources and 348 IceCube high-energy track alerts is statistically consistent with random background.
summary.novel_idea: The paper performs the first systematic spatial correlation and hadronic flux comparison between the complete First LHAASO Catalog of 90 VHE/UHE gamma-ray sources and IceCube's IceCat-1 alert track dataset ($E_\nu \ge 100\text{ TeV}$).
summary.method: Spatial coincidences are defined by the geometric intersection of LHAASO containment radii (combining 2D-Gaussian $r_{39}$ and centroid errors) with IceCat-1 $90\%$ angular error regions. Statistical significance is evaluated via 10,000 Monte Carlo pseudo-experiments randomizing neutrino right ascensions while preserving declination-dependent acceptance. Optimistic hadronic neutrino fluxes are calculated assuming purely $pp$-driven gamma-ray emission and compared to single-event Poisson upper limits.
key_results: Identified 9 spatial coincidences involving 7 neutrino events and 8 LHAASO sources under the primary cut $\Omega_{90} \le 10\text{ deg}^2$.
Obtained post-trial p-values of 0.237 for the full source catalog, 0.312 for KM2A sources, and 0.115 for WCDA sources, failing to reject the null hypothesis of chance coincidence.
Demonstrated that the most optimistic hadronic neutrino fluxes for candidate sources fall below the sensitivity threshold required to produce IceCat-1 alert triggers.
summary.why_it_matters: The analysis constrains Galactic PeVatron neutrino production but lies outside the reader's primary focus on neutrino-nucleus scattering mechanisms, generator physics, and low-energy neutrino phenomenology.
summary.caveats: The search utilizes a simple geometric overlap metric rather than an unbinned likelihood analysis with per-event reconstruction PSFs, and only considers high-energy alert tracks rather than IceCube's full point-source archival track dataset.

papers.title: Transient PULSE: Code for the Transient Propagation of UltraLight (pseudo)Scalars to Earth
papers.abstract: We present Transient PULSE, a software package that numerically implements a previously developed source-to-detector framework for transient ultralight bosonic signals from astrophysical bursts. Predicting these signals relies on connecting the source emission spectrum to its evolution during propagation and the resulting observables at a terrestrial detector. The package discretizes a user supplied energy spectrum into momentum modes, propagates them through a specified matter density profile and constructs the time-frequency energy density distribution at Earth, accounting for dispersion and in-medium screening effects. This treatment accommodates non-Gaussian source spectra and provides inputs for detector specific analyses. A complementary analytical module estimates coupling sensitivities, arrival time delays and screening thresholds from parameterized source and detector properties.
papers.reason: Presents a numerical code for transient ultralight bosonic signals from astrophysical bursts reaching terrestrial detectors, relevant to BSM searches at neutrino experiments.

summary.tldr: Presents Transient PULSE, a Python software package that simulates the propagation, dispersion, and medium-screening of transient ultralight scalar and pseudoscalar bursts from astrophysical transients to terrestrial detectors.
summary.novel_idea: The package provides the first public end-to-end numerical and analytical framework for propagating transient ultralight bosonic fields through realistic galactic matter profiles, coupling non-Gaussian source emission spectra directly to time-frequency spectrograms and terrestrial sensor limits.
summary.method: The numerical engine discretizes arbitrary source energy spectra into momentum modes and integrates the one-dimensional relativistic dispersion relation through user-defined density profiles, incorporating in-medium effective mass shifts and screening cutoffs. An analytical module computes detection sensitivities by rescaling steady-state dark matter limits from atomic clocks, magnetometers, and fifth-force experiments to finite-duration coherent bursts.
key_results: Verifies energy conservation across kiloparsec propagation baselines to better than $1\%$ for benchmark bosenova spectra.
Demonstrates linear runtime scaling with the number of time and momentum grid points ($<1\text{ s}$ for $10^3 \times 10^3$ grids).
Provides modular workflows for evaluating linear and quadratic scalar couplings to electrons, photons, and gluons, as well as ALP derivative couplings to nucleons and spins.
summary.why_it_matters: Touches upon precision atomic physics and quantum sensor techniques for BSM searches, but is unrelated to neutrino-nucleus cross sections, neutrino experiments, or accelerator neutrino beamlines.
summary.caveats: The current numerical propagation engine assumes spherical symmetry and neglects non-linear field self-interactions during propagation.

papers.title: Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory and its application to $X_b$
papers.abstract: Following the discovery of the exotic state $X(3872)$ in the charmonium spectrum, the possible existence of an analogous state, $X_b$, in the bottomonium sector has attracted considerable attention of the hadronic physics community. In this work, we lay the ground for the development of Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory (BO$\chi$EFT), that allows us to include both quark and hadron degrees of freedom as well as the full complexity of the meson-exchange potential in a systematic way. For illustration, the formalism to leading order (LO) is applied to the system of $\chi_{b1}$ states and in particular the $X_b$. The two parameters that are present at this order are constrained using experimental information on the bottomonium spectrum together with lattice input on static quark-antiquark potentials, including string breaking effects. The framework identifies the observed $1^{++}$ state at 10.513 GeV with a predominantly molecular $X_b$, the bottom counterpart of the $X(3872)$, and predicts an additional predominantly compact bottomonium state at 10.544 GeV, about 60 MeV below the $B\bar{B}^*$ threshold.
papers.reason: Develops Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory incorporating meson-exchange potentials for bottomonium/charmonium exotic states, relevant to advanced hadronic interactions and nuclear forces.

summary.tldr: Formulates Born-Oppenheimer chiral EFT in momentum space to describe the $1^{++}$ bottomonium spectrum, predicting that the observed $\chi_{b1}(3P)$ is a molecular $X_b$ and identifying an undiscovered compact partner.
summary.novel_idea: The work develops Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory (BO$\chi$EFT) in momentum space, merging unquenched lattice-QCD static quark-antiquark potentials (including string-breaking couplings) with a systematic chiral meson-exchange potential (including singular tensor forces and contact terms) in a coupled-channel Lippmann-Schwinger framework.
summary.method: The authors solve coupled-channel Lippmann-Schwinger equations combining bare $\bar{b}b(nP)$ states with $B\bar{B}^*$ and $B^*\bar{B}^*$ continuum channels. String-breaking transition matrix elements are taken from lattice QCD in the static limit, while light pseudoscalar meson exchanges are computed with chiral EFT power counting. Two free parameters (the static potential energy offset $V_0$ and an S-wave contact term $C$) are fixed using the masses of the three known axial-vector $\chi_{b1}$ states.
key_results: Identifies the physical state at $10513.4\text{ MeV}$ (currently assigned to $\chi_{b1}(3P)$) as a predominantly molecular $X_b$ state ($98\%$ hadronic compositeness: $41\%$ S-wave, $36\%$ D-wave, and $21\%$ 3-body).

Predicts the existence of a predominantly compact $\chi_{b1}(3P)$ bottomonium state at $10.544\text{ GeV}$ ($10\text{--}17\%$ hadronic compositeness), roughly $60\text{ MeV}$ below the $B\bar{B}^*$ threshold.
Identifies and successfully projects out a regulator-induced spurious deep bound state arising from the attractive chiral tensor force without shifting physical low-energy observables.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides technical insights into non-perturbative chiral EFT methods, coupled-channel Lippmann-Schwinger equations, and the regularization of singular tensor forces, but focuses entirely on heavy quarkonium exotic spectroscopy rather than neutrino physics.
summary.caveats: Short-range contact counterterms cannot yet be systematically matched between the charm and bottom sectors due to unconstrained heavy-quark mass scaling in four-hadron operators.

papers.title: Constraints on pion parton distributions at small $x$ from leading-neutron electroproduction data
papers.abstract: We revisit the extraction of parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the pion in a global QCD analysis of pion--nucleus Drell--Yan and leading-neutron (LN) electroproduction data, in view of recent suggestions that uncertainties on the pion PDFs at small parton momentum fraction $x$ are dramatically underestimated. We perform a set of controlled fits that vary the LN data coverage, PDF parametrization, and positivity constraints, determining both the PDFs and pion-nucleon splitting functions simultaneously. While the use of a restricted H1 LN data sample used by the Fant\^omas group is found to enlarge the PDF uncertainties and admit solutions with vanishing gluon PDFs, our global analysis provides a good description of an extended H1 and ZEUS LN database, significantly reducing the parametrization dependence and strongly disfavoring a zero gluon distribution.
papers.reason: Global QCD analysis of pion parton distribution functions using leading-neutron electroproduction data, highly relevant to understanding pion structure and neutrino-induced pion production backgrounds.

papers.title: The Semileptonic B Frontier: LHC, B-factories, Lattice QCD & the Hunt for Precision
papers.abstract: This review document summarizes the main outcomes and key theoretical and experimental developments discussed at the workshop ``The Semileptonic $B$ Frontier: LHC, $B$-Factories, Lattice QCD & the Hunt for Precision'', held at Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati on 16--18 February, https://agenda.infn.it/event/49469/. Bringing together experimentalists and theorists, the meeting addressed recent advances and outstanding challenges in both charged-current ($b \to c/u\,\ell\nu$) and neutral-current ($b \to s\,\ell^+\ell^-$) semileptonic $b$-hadron decays. We synthesize current experimental measurements from Belle, Belle~II, and LHCb with state-of-the-art theoretical inputs---including Lattice QCD determinations, Heavy Quark Expansion (HQE) frameworks, and QED radiative corrections. In addition to reviewing the status of CKM matrix elements, hadronic form factor extractions, and Lepton Flavor Universality (LFU) tests, this report highlights novel observables and fitting techniques designed to maximize the sensitivity of future analyses and guide upcoming data-taking campaigns.
papers.reason: Comprehensive workshop review on semileptonic B decays, lattice QCD, CKM matrix elements, and form factor extractions, highly relevant to precision electroweak and heavy-flavor inputs.

papers.title: The dead-cone effect in charm, bottom and top quark jets in angular and momentum space
papers.abstract: The dead-cone effect reflects the mass dependence of QCD radiation from heavy quarks. We investigate this phenomenon from charm and bottom to top quarks using two-dimensional angular distributions and single-particle inclusive momentum spectra. The angular distributions illustrate the depletion of radiation around the heavy-quark direction, while the momentum spectra provide a quantitative observable of the effect. For charm and bottom jets, fragmentation functions reconstructed from LEP data at the $Z$ pole exhibit a strong suppression of high-momentum particles, quantitatively described within the Modified Leading Logarithmic Approximation of perturbative QCD. The analysis is extended to $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV using Monte Carlo simulations. A hypothetical stable-top sample isolates the primary top-quark radiation pattern, whereas the physical decay $t\to bW$ introduces coherent radiation from the $tb$ colour dipole, obscuring the primary dead cone. By exploiting the dependence on the $b$-quark emission angle $\Theta_b$, we reconstruct the primary top-quark parton momentum spectrum through extrapolation to $\Theta_b\to0$. In contrast, the small-angle gluon and parton distributions do not converge to the stable-top dead-cone pattern because of radiation from the decay $b$ quark. These findings establish the inclusive momentum spectrum as a robust quantitative observable of the top-quark dead-cone effect and provide a unified description of mass-dependent QCD radiation from charm to top.
papers.reason: Investigates the mass-dependent dead-cone effect in charm, bottom, and top quark jets using angular distributions and momentum spectra, closely aligned with perturbative QCD and heavy-quark fragmentation.

papers.title: Spin and 3D structure: theoretical advances
papers.abstract: Theoretical studies of hadron structure have made important progress since the previous DIS workshop in 2025. This talk reviews selected new results and developments, with a focus on spin dependent parton distributions, on transverse-momentum distributions and their rapidity dependence, on generalised parton distributions, and on the evaluation of power corrections.
papers.reason: Review of theoretical advances in spin-dependent parton distributions, transverse-momentum distributions, GPDs, and power corrections, highly relevant to nucleon structure functions.

papers.title: Brownian GPDs: A Stochastic Calculus Approach to Generalized Parton Distributions from Integral Constraints
papers.abstract: We present a stochastic calculus approach for modeling generalized parton distribution functions using information provided from lattice QCD calculations of Mellin moments, without assuming a functional form. Reconstructing the underlying dependence on the partonic momentum fraction from a limited number of moments constitutes an intrinsically non-unique inverse problem. Our goal is to provide a model agnostic way to determine GPDs subject to integral constraints. Thus, we derive and show usage of a controlled Langevin approach based on stochastic calculus and Brownian motion. The method combines a variational formulation, based on minimizing a Dirichlet action subject to the imposed constraints, with stochastic dynamics that generates an ensemble of admissible functions. The resulting ensemble provides a preferred reconstruction and characterizes the variability associated with incomplete integral information within the chosen stochastic model. The framework can accommodate general integral kernels and prescribed function values, offering a flexible approach to reconstructing functions from indirect constraints. Beyond its application to GPD phenomenology, the method provides a general strategy for investigating inverse problems in which integral observables are known but the underlying functional dependence remains undetermined. The approach may have more general applications beyond the scope of studying 3D hadron structure, and it is particularly useful in situations where we know definite integrals of functions with kernels, but do not know the underlying function.
papers.reason: Presents a stochastic calculus and Langevin approach for modeling generalized parton distributions from lattice QCD moments without assuming rigid functional forms.

papers.title: Measurement of electromagnetic transition form factors in two-photon collisions at BESIII
papers.abstract: The muon anomalous magnetic moment, $a_\mu = (g-2)_\mu/2$, shows a sizeable discrepancy between Standard Model (SM) predictions and direct measurements, hinting at either New Physics or limitations in modeling low-energy strong interactions. As the uncertainty in the SM predictions currently exceeds the experimental uncertainty by a substantial margin, further improvements in theoretical precision are essential to clarify the origin of this discrepancy. The SM theoretical uncertainty is dominated by hadronic processes. The hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution relies on highly accurate data for hadron production via two-photon fusion. Operating at $\sqrt{s}=3.773\,\text{GeV}$ with over $20\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity, the BESIII experiment is ideally suited to probe these processes at small momentum transfers. By precisely measuring channels like $e^+e^-\to e^+ e^-\pi^0$ and $e^+e^-\to e^+ e^-\pi^0\pi^0$, BESIII provides the critical experimental input necessary to sharpen the SM prediction and clarify the true nature of the $a_\mu$ anomaly.
authors: Max Lellmann (on behalf of the BESIII collaboration)
papers.reason: Reviews electromagnetic transition form factors and hadronic light-by-light scattering inputs from two-photon collisions at BESIII, essential for reducing hadronic uncertainties in electroweak and muon $g-2$ contexts.

papers.title: Stabilizer R\'enyi Entropy Without a Phase Reference
papers.abstract: Stabilizer R\'enyi entropy quantifies magic relative to a complete Pauli frame. In settings such as helicity states of massless particles, unsynchronized qubit registers, energy eigenbases, and systems under superselection rules, the computational basis may be fixed while the transverse Pauli axes remain unspecified. The stabilizer R\'enyi entropy then depends on the choice of those axes. We define a phase-averaged stabilizer R\'enyi entropy by averaging the Pauli moments before taking the logarithm. It is exactly invariant under independent local rephasings. For pure states, it vanishes precisely when the state is a stabilizer state in every phase convention. For a broad class of sparse supports, it reduces to a closed-form function of the basis-state probabilities alone. Within this class, the ceiling for $n$ channels is $\ln[n^{3}/(6n-5)]$ for $n\geq3$ and $\ln\frac{7}{5}$ for two channels. We apply the invariant to tree-level gluon scattering at four and five points, where the helicity-basis phases are unspecified. It saturates the two- and three-channel ceilings: $\ln\frac{7}{5}$ at four points and $\ln\frac{27}{13}$ in $3\to2$ scattering. In same-helicity $2\to3$ scattering, it lies between a floor of $\ln\frac{8}{7}$ and a ceiling of $\ln\frac{184}{125}$, reached in the resolved soft limit and particular collinear limits, respectively. In every configuration studied, the invariant is independent of the fixed external colors.
papers.reason: Introduces a phase-invariant stabilizer Rènyi entropy applied to tree-level multi-particle gluon and helicity scattering amplitudes.

papers.title: Constraint on particle mass of dark matter based on XTE J1814-338 observation and DANS model
papers.abstract: The small observed radius of neutron star XTE J1814-338 (with mass of $1.21_{-0.05}^{+0.05}$ $M_{\odot}$ and radius of $7_{-0.4}^{+0.4}$ $\rm{km}$) poses a great challenge to the traditional neutron star model composed of normal nuclear matter. The dark matter admixed neutron star (DANS) model provides a clue to solve this challenge. By employing the self-interacting fermionic dark matter model, we investigate the effects of dark matter parameters including the particle mass, self-interaction strength, and mass fraction of dark matter on the properties of DANSs. Our results indicate that the joint constraints from the observation of XTE J1814-338 and the astrophysical limits on the dark matter self-interaction cross section derived from observations of different colliding galaxy clusters can provide effective constraints on the particle mass of dark matter. Specifically, to simultaneously satisfy the small radius of XTE J1814-338 and the self-interaction limit, the particle mass of self-interacting fermionic dark matter is constrained to the range from sub-GeV to a few GeV.
papers.topic: Dark matter particle mass from NS
papers.reason: Uses neutron star observations (XTE J1814-338) and dark matter admixture models to constrain sub-GeV to GeV dark matter particle masses.

papers.title: Prospects for modelling odd and odd-odd nuclei using energy density functionals
papers.abstract: About half of particle-bound nuclei have an odd number of nucleons. About one quarter more are odd-odd, meaning they have an odd number of neutrons and an odd number of protons. In this context, it is about time to shift the 70-odd-year focus of theories using nuclear energy density functionals (EDFs) away from the remaining one-quarter of even-even nuclei. This White Paper aims to present open, unresolved problems and promising research directions in nuclear EDFs that were discussed during the 2024 ESNT workshop in Saclay, France, on ``The microscopic modelling of odd-mass and odd-odd nuclei''.
papers.reason: Examines microscopic modeling of odd and odd-odd nuclei using EDFs, providing relevant nuclear structure context for neutrino-nucleus interaction calculations.

papers.title: A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation
papers.abstract: Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. We present a low-cost, compact muon detector consisting of two plastic scintillator modules, each read out by a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), operated in coincidence. We characterize the SiPMs from room temperature down to 10 mK, including the breakdown and upper-limit voltages that define the operating bias range. Operated as a muon counter, the detector measures a coincidence rate that, as expected, is independent of temperature within uncertainties and agrees with analytical and Monte Carlo predictions. Below approximately 8 K, each muon event produces two pulses, one narrow and one broad, an effect that, to our knowledge, has not been reported before. Coincidences with an independent muon detector outside the cryostat confirm that muons are still counted reliably in this regime. By studying the appearance of double pulses as a function of temperature and magnetic field up to 4.5 T, we find a behavior consistent with the phase diagram of a type-II superconductor. This links the double pulses to a superconducting material in the SiPM, likely an adhesion layer or diffusion barrier introduced during manufacturing. The mechanism by which the superconducting state produces the second pulse is not yet understood.
papers.reason: Presents a low-cost compact muon detector operating at millikelvin temperatures inside dilution refrigerators to tag cosmic ray muons for superconducting qubit error mitigation.

papers.title: Exothermic dark-photon dark matter and the LZ high-recoil event: finite-reheating constraints
papers.abstract: An excited dark-matter state can produce a high-energy nuclear recoil by releasing its mass splitting in a collision. Motivated by the $248$~keV LUX--ZEPLIN candidate, we study freeze-in of a $45$~GeV pseudo-Dirac particle with a $1$~MeV splitting and a $1$~GeV dark photon during non-instantaneous reheating. We choose a recoil normalization compatible with the published INTEGRAL/SPI three-photon decay limit. It predicts $0.43$ events in the LZ window and retains the reference recoil shape. Including both dark-photon and $Z$ exchange, we calculate production and entropy dilution for backgrounds with $T\propto a^{-\alpha}$ and $\rho_\phi\propto a^{-3(1+\omega)}$. For $\Tmax=m_\chi$, the observed abundance requires $\Trh=1.32$~GeV for matter-like constant-width reheating, $3.09$~GeV for quartic oscillations with scalar decay, and $0.588$~GeV for quartic oscillations with constant width, compared with $4.10$~GeV for instantaneous reheating. These finite-reheating solutions are insensitive to increasing $\Tmax$ above $m_\chi$. For $\Tmax\geq m_\chi$, adiabatic kination has no solution with $\Trh>5.96$~MeV, the BBN-motivated cutoff adopted for our scans. At $\alpha_D=10^{-10}$, the estimated thermal-mediator source is below $0.2\%$ of the Standard Model source, and self-conversion does not appreciably deplete the excited population. The calculation relates an exothermic recoil benchmark to the production and dilution history before radiation domination.
papers.reason: Examines freeze-in and finite-reheating constraints for an exothermic dark matter candidate linked to the LZ high-recoil event, intersecting with direct detection backgrounds.

papers.title: Bottom-Charm $[bc]$ Diquark Masses from QCD Laplace Sum-Rules
papers.abstract: Constituent mass predictions for bottom-charm $[bc]$ color-antitriplet diquarks are generated using QCD Laplace sum rules. We calculate the diquark correlator within the operator product expansion to next-to-leading-order (NLO), including terms proportional to the four- and six-dimensional gluon and six-dimensional quark condensates. Existing analytic expressions for the resulting multi-scale master integrals are insufficient for these calculations, so we utilize numerical $D$-dimensional loop integration techniques. The sum rule analyses stabilize in all four channels yielding constituent masses in GeV of: scalar ($0^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$, pseudoscalar ($0^-$) $(6.04\pm0.60)$, axial vector ($1^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$ and vector ($1^-$) $(5.99\pm0.60)$. These constituent mass results are discussed in comparison with values used in diquark models of tetraquark hadronic states. We also summarize QCD sum rule predictions for diquark masses for all possible quark-flavor combinations, providing QCD-based criteria for assessing the diquark mass parameters used in constituent diquark models of hadrons.
papers.reason: Calculates bottom-charm diquark masses using QCD Laplace sum rules, providing inputs for multi-quark hadronic states relevant to nonperturbative QCD.

papers.title: Binding energies in the $0^{-+}$ and $1^{--}$ fermion--antifermion channels from the ladder Bethe-Salpeter and Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract: In this work, we calculate the binding energies of an equal-mass fermion--antifermion system in the $0^{-+}$ and $1^{--}$ channels from the ladder Bethe--Salpeter (BS) equation with scalar, pseudoscalar, and vector exchange. The results are compared with those of the Schr\"odinger equation with the corresponding leading static interaction in two regimes: pointlike massless exchange at weak coupling and finite-mass exchange with monopole form factors at stronger coupling. For the BS calculation, we use two independent numerical methods based on momentum-space integral equations and coordinate-space differential equations. The differential-equation method gives estimated relative binding-energy errors below $10^{-9}$ in both regimes. For massless vector exchange in Coulomb gauge, the numerical results are consistent with the uncrossed-ladder perturbative spectrum through the $O(m\alpha^5)$ terms. The results for massless scalar exchange and vector exchange in Feynman gauge are consistent with the common Wick--Cutkosky expansion through order $m\alpha^3$. For finite exchange masses, the differences from the leading static Schr\"odinger spectra at the same masses, couplings, and form factors depend strongly on the exchange and channel. Scalar exchange gives nearly degenerate channels with much weaker binding than the Schr\"odinger reference. In contrast, vector exchange with only the metric term retained gives stronger binding than the Schr\"odinger reference in $0^{-+}$ and weaker binding in $1^{--}$. Notably, retaining the full Proca numerator substantially increases the vector binding in both channels. Pseudoscalar exchange also supports bound states and favors $1^{--}$, although its leading static central interaction vanishes.
papers.reason: Calculates binding energies of fermion-antifermion systems using ladder Bethe-Salpeter and Schrödinger equations, useful for understanding bound-state dynamics and potential models.

papers.title: Decoherence as a Detector-Resolution Flow
papers.abstract: We consider the QED final-state radiation modeled by $\gamma\gamma^\ast\to\pi^+\pi^-+X$, including its finite-temperature generalization, as an open quantum system, and study the evolution of the pion-pair momentum density matrix as the detector resolution scale is varied. We derive an explicit relation between the Lindblad jump operator and the Wilson line associated with soft photon radiation. We find that real emission and virtual correction serve as two separate contributions to momentum decoherence, and together they give rise to the real--virtual cancellation at the density-matrix level. The external finite-temperature photon bath modifies the decoherence rate by a Bose factor consistent with the Feynman--Vernon influence-functional approach. We emphasize that our conclusions also apply to hard fermion production thanks to the universality of the soft radiation.
papers.reason: Models QED final-state radiation and open quantum system decoherence as a detector-resolution flow, touching on quantum coherence and final states.

papers.title: Transport of hard probes in the glasma
papers.abstract: The quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formed in relativistic heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC thermalizes from an out-of-equilibrium state of strong classical gluon fields known as the glasma. Jets and heavy quarks, produced in the initial scatterings, traverse these pre-equilibrium fields, but the glasma stage is neglected in phenomenology, which may bias the extracted QGP transport coefficients. This thesis studies its impact on jet and heavy quark transport. The glasma is described in the Color Glass Condensate framework by solving the classical Yang-Mills equations on a real-time lattice. The fields initially form longitudinal electric and magnetic flux tubes whose transverse correlation length is set by the saturation scale $Q_s$. Probes are studied with both classical transport equations and quantum evolution in the light-front Hamiltonian approach. The transport coefficients for jets and heavy quarks are much larger than in the QGP and anisotropic between transverse and longitudinal directions. The azimuthal decorrelation of back-to-back $c\bar{c}$ pairs in the glasma is comparable to that from the QGP, making $D\bar{D}$ angular correlations a potentially measurable glasma signature. The glasma also modifies the nuclear modification factor $R_{AA}$, though the effect is moderate compared to the nuclear parton distribution contribution. A systematic gauge-invariance analysis shows that the distinction between kinetic and canonical momenta is essential when comparing classical and quantum results, and that Coulomb gauge fixing largely reduces gauge artifacts. Finally, the eikonal quantum evolution of a high-energy quark is studied with time-dependent Basis Light-Front Quantization. The resulting momentum broadening agrees with the classical estimates and lays the groundwork for including quantum radiation.
papers.reason: Studies jet and heavy quark transport through the glasma stage of heavy-ion collisions using classical Yang-Mills equations and light-front Hamiltonian methods.

papers.title: Evolution of multihadron fragmentation functions with nonperturbative behavior
papers.abstract: QCD calculations that use multihadron fragmentation functions usually involve multiple invariant mass scales simultaneously, with only one being the hard scale associated with an overall hard process. The other scales are associated with relative internal motion intrinsic to the fragmenting parton and the multihadron system. Nonperturbative contributions to this later type of dependence attract interest for their association with intrinsic partonic structures, but care is needed in disentangling the truly nonperturbative effects from perturbative behavior and relating the former to universal nonperturbative matrix elements. To this end, we show how to evolve collinear multihadron fragmentation functions in a way that accounts for the simultaneous presence of these extra scales. The general multihadron fragmentation functions evolve in the same way as ordinary single hadron fragmentation functions, with the dependence on the extra scales separated out. We use this to unify treatments of perturbative and nonperturbative effects in multihadron systems in a way that optimizes for interpretations focused on partonic structure.
papers.reason: Develops a formalism to evolve collinear multihadron fragmentation functions while separating out intrinsic mass scales and nonperturbative partonic structures.

papers.title: Two-loop $gg\to AA$ amplitudes near threshold and the double parton scattering singularity
papers.abstract: The two-loop amplitudes for pseudoscalar pair production in gluon fusion, $gg\to AA$, with each pseudoscalar emitted from its own effective gluon vertex, are known in closed form, but large cancellations near threshold obscure their analytic structure. We expand the IR-finite amplitudes in the pseudoscalar velocity $\beta_A$ through $\beta_A^6$ at fixed scattering angle. All inverse powers of $\beta_A$ and the odd powers through $\beta_A^5$ cancel, and at leading power the angular dependence enters only through $\ln(2p_T/m_A)$. We identify this logarithm with the double parton scattering (DPS) singularity: with the overall constant fixed at threshold, the factorisation formula of Gaunt and Stirling reproduces the velocity dependence of its one-loop coefficient in the forward limit to $3\times10^{-15}$, and a one-loop $gg\to HH$ analysis confirms the corresponding CP-even weight. At two loops the equal-helicity amplitude grows as $\ln^3p_T$, with the leading logarithmic ratio of planar $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, while the opposite helicity amplitude, which has no one-loop DPS logarithm, grows as $\ln^2p_T$. In the finite virtual correction, relative to the squared tree amplitude, the highest logarithm at order $\alpha_s^2$ is $-\tfrac{7}{64}\alpha_s^2N_c^2\ln^2(2p_T/m_A)$. For $\beta_A\leq0.2$ the series reproduce the unexpanded amplitudes with relative errors of at most $6.77\times10^{-5}$ at the tested points; they provide this two-loop contribution to the hard function for soft-gluon resummation of the pair invariant-mass distribution near $m_{AA}=2m_A$ and are released with code for their numerical evaluation.
papers.reason: Analyzes two-loop amplitudes and double parton scattering singularities for pseudoscalar production in gluon fusion, touching on perturbative QCD factorization.

papers.title: Effective Fermion-Photon Vertex in a Rotating Relativistic Medium: Tree-Level Structure
papers.abstract: We study the tree-level fermion-photon effective vertex for on-shell particles in a relativistic environment undergoing rigid rotation at zero temperature. The rotational background breaks translational invariance in the transverse plane and introduces a preferred direction, leading to a distinct decomposition of the vertex into longitudinal and transverse structures with respect to the rotation axis. Using fermion and photon modes constructed in the rotating frame, we derive the corresponding selection rules and show that the energy and the longitudinal component of the momentum are conserved, whereas no independent transverse momentum-conservation condition arises. Instead, the transverse dependence is governed by radial integrals involving three Bessel functions, whose support constrains the magnitudes of the transverse momentum projections. The vertex can be organized in a circular basis for the transverse components and a Cartesian basis along the rotation axis, and expressed in terms of six Dirac structures. Their coefficients define 24 form-factor components associated with the photon-mode components, physical photon states, and spin-dependent structures induced by the rotating background. We also verify current conservation and gauge invariance of the resulting tree-level matrix element under the boundary conditions considered. These results provide the tree-level structure of the fermion-photon interaction in rotating relativistic matter and establish the basis for the study of radiative corrections in vortical backgrounds.
papers.reason: Evaluates the tree-level fermion-photon effective vertex in a rigidly rotating relativistic medium, touching on quantum field theory under external conditions.

papers.title: Strange-quark-number-dependent response to partonic dynamics in baryon-rich Au+Au collisions
papers.abstract: We identify a strange-quark-number-dependent hierarchy in the response to explicit partonic dynamics by comparing PHSD5.2 with its hadron--string limit in baryon-rich Au+Au collisions at $\snn=3.0$--$7.2$~GeV. Crossing the local conversion threshold alone does not ensure a visible final-state signal: abundant-hadron flow changes little at 3--4.5~GeV, whereas the fractional yield response becomes ordered at 6.2--7.2~GeV, reaching $S_{|s|=1}\simeq0.2$--$0.3$, $S_{|s|=2}\simeq0.65$, and $S_{|s|=3}\simeq0.93$ at 7.2~GeV. The hierarchy is consistent with an enlarged recombination phase space for strange constituents released from different pre-hadronic sources, but does not by itself establish an increase in the total $s+\bar s$ abundance or stronger strange-quark clustering. Since $S_X$ is a model-defined response rather than a direct observable, matched excitation functions of $\Xi^-/\Lambda$ and $\Omega^-/\Lambda$, together with high-$m_T$ proton elliptic flow, provide experimentally accessible discriminants between the predicted PHSD and HSD dynamics.
papers.reason: Identifies strange-quark-number-dependent responses to partonic dynamics in heavy-ion collisions, relevant to nuclear matter transport and strangeness production.

papers.title: Thermal spectral functions of heavy and exotic Mesons from a hQCD at finite density
papers.abstract: In this work, we study spectral functions of heavy and exotic mesons in a self-consistent Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton model at finite temperature and chemical potential, where the dilaton is allowed to back-react on the geometry. A non-quadratic dilaton profile is introduced to reproduce the nonlinear Regge trajectories of heavy-flavor mesons, and the corresponding spectral functions are computed for charmonium, bottomonium, tetraquark, and hybrid channels. In all cases, increasing either temperature or chemical potential suppresses and broadens the quasiparticle peaks, signaling sequential in-medium dissociation; for each radial family, the 2S-like state melts before the 1S-like state. The predicted melting temperatures obey the mass ordering $T_{\rm melt}^{\pi_1(1400)}<T_{\rm melt}^{J/\psi}<T_{\rm melt}^{Z_c(3900)}<T_{\rm melt}^{\Upsilon(1S)}$, with $T_{\rm melt}\simeq 1.08,\ 2.96,\ 4.44$, and $5.93\,T_c$, respectively, so heavier states remain bound up to higher temperatures. These results provide quantitative, testable predictions for heavy-ion experiments probing tetraquark and hybrid mesons in hot and dense QCD matter.
papers.reason: Computes thermal spectral functions for heavy and exotic mesons using a holographic Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton model at finite density.

papers.title: R-process nuclei in the rare-earth region above N=126 in Relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory: A preponderance of shape-coexistence in nuclei
papers.abstract: The shell structure of nuclei beyond N=126 relevant to the third peak at A ~ 195 in r-process nuclear abundances in investigated. Within the framework of the relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in deformed space, a comparative study of the response of nuclei with three different model Lagrangians NL-SV1, SVI-2 and NL3 is made. Ground-state properties of even-even nuclei in the isotopic chains of Z=58-72$= in the highly neutron-rich region are investigated. A comparison of binding energies with mass formulas shows that in the extreme region of the r-process path, the RMF model SVI-2 without nonlinearities of sigma and omega mesons shows an excellent agreement with the mass formula HFB-24. It is shown that in all the above Lagrangian models, in the neutron rich region between the shell closures N=126 and N=184, there is a preponderance of nuclides exhibiting coexistence of well-deformed prolate and oblate shapes in the ground state. A prolate ground state is shown to evolve smoothly to a coexisting oblate ground state via a near degeneracy with successive addition of neutrons. Induced by an onset of deformation for $N \ge 130$, nuclei approaching the r-process path are shown to exhibit enhanced stability in many isotopic chains (Z > 60). This has the effect of shifting the expected neutron drip line significantly farther into the neutron-rich region especially for the higher Z chains. Consequences of the enhanced stability, the shape co-existence and degeneracy of shapes in nuclei on the r-process nucleosynthesis are discussed.
papers.reason: Investigates shape coexistence and shell structure in extreme neutron-rich nuclei near the r-process path using relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory.

papers.title: Collective-flow signatures of bubble nuclei in intermediate-energy projectile fragmentation reactions
papers.abstract: Characterized by central density depletion, bubble nuclei represent an important class of exotic nuclear structures. Collective flow in the $^{40}$Ca+$^{9}$Be projectile fragmentation reaction at 140 MeV/u is investigated using the extended quantum molecular dynamics (EQMD) model with a parameter on of the isoscalar monopole excitation strength $\varepsilon$. The projectile $^{40}Ca$ is initialized as a relaxed ten-$\alpha$ cluster configuration exhibiting a bubble-like density distribution. The results reveal that increasing $\varepsilon$ modifies the density distribution and the size of the depleted central region of bubble, producing pronounced changes in fragment yields and collective flow around $\varepsilon\approx0.5$. Below this value, heavy-fragment production plays a significant role, while the directed flow $v_1$ of protons and neutrons remains predominantly negative, indicating preferential emission toward the target side. Above $\varepsilon\approx0.5$, enhanced expansion of the central low-density region suppresses heavy residues and drives $v_1$ toward positive values. In contrast, preformed $\alpha$ clusters show different responses, reflecting their origin in the initial cluster configuration rather than solely in secondary decay. At low excitation, the cluster flow exhibits a pronounced impact-parameter dependence, whereas stronger excitation weakens cluster binding and suppresses directional anisotropy, driving the flow close to zero. The rapidity slopes of the flow coefficients also vary systematically with $\varepsilon$, tracing changes in emission anisotropy during expansion. These findings extend traditional static descriptions by probing the dynamical evolution of exotic structures in heavy-ion reactions and the contrasting collective-flow behavior of preformed clusters and single nucleons constitutes a sensitive dynamical probe of bubble-like structures.
papers.reason: Investigates collective flow and fragment yields of bubble nuclei in intermediate-energy projectile fragmentation using quantum molecular dynamics.

papers.title: Achieving a 0.49 keV threshold in the COSINE-100 dark matter experiment
papers.abstract: The COSINE-100 experiment searched for weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) with NaI(Tl) crystals at the Yangyang Underground Laboratory. Using its full 6-year dataset, we lower the analysis threshold to 0.49 keV. A multi-layer perceptron classifier separates scintillation events from photomultiplier tube noise. It is trained with approximately $3\times10^{6}$ simulated scintillation waveforms per crystal, separately for groups of events with similar numbers of photoelectron clusters. The selection keeps more than 10% of scintillation events at 0.49 keV while limiting noise contamination to below 1%. The selection efficiency is validated with $^{22}$Na-calibration data and internal $^{22}$Na events, and the selection performance is stable over the six years of data taking. With this threshold, the median expected upper limit on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section reaches $1.1\times10^{-36}$ cm$^2$ at a WIMP mass of 2.5 GeV/$c^2$, probing previously unexplored parameter space in the 2.0-2.8 GeV/$c^2$ mass range.
authors: D. F. F. S. Cavalcante (COSINE-100 Collaboration)
papers.reason: Achieves a 0.49 keV threshold in the COSINE-100 dark matter experiment using machine learning waveform classification, relevant to low-energy nuclear recoil detection techniques.

papers.title: Measurement of Born cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\bar\Sigma^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.5-4.9 GeV and partial wave analysis at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV
papers.abstract: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 44.6 $\rm fb^{-1}$, we present the first measurement of the Born cross sections for the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ + c.c. at fifty-six center-of-mass energies between 3.51 and 4.95~GeV. By fitting the dressed cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ + c.c. with the assumption of a power-law function plus a charmonium(-like) resonance, i.e., $\psi(3770)$, $\psi(4040)$, $\psi(4160)$, $Y(4230)$, $Y(4360)$, $\psi(4415)$, $\psi(4500)$, $Y(4660)$ or $\psi(4710)$, no significant charmonium(-like) state decaying into $pK^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ + c.c. is observed. The product of branching fractions and electronic partial widths including their upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are provided for each decay. In addition, a partial wave analysis of the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV is performed to investigate $N^{*}$, $\Lambda^{*}$ and $\Sigma^{*}$ resonances in the $K^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ and $pK^{-}$ invariant mass spectra. Significant contributions are found from the $\Lambda(1520)$, $\Sigma(1670)$, $\Sigma(1915)$, $N(1900)$, $N(2300)$ and $N(2570)$. The masses, widths and production fractions for each component are determined.

papers.title: Thermal properties of the $\rho$ meson from a machine-learning-improved holographic QCD model
papers.abstract: The thermal properties of the \(\rho\) meson are revisited within the soft-wall AdS/QCD framework. The dilaton background is calibrated against lattice QCD screening-mass data through a neural-network-assisted inverse procedure. Using this calibrated background, we compute the temporal vector spectral function and the lowest vector quasi-normal modes. The pole mass \(m_{\mathrm{pole}}(T)\) and thermal width \(\Gamma(T)\) are then extracted from the corresponding complex quasi-normal mode frequencies. Adopting the vanishing real part of the quasi-normal mode frequency, \(\omega_{\mathrm{Re}}(T_d)=0\), as a criterion for meson dissociation, we estimate \(T_d\approx168\,\mathrm{MeV}\). As the temperature increases, the thermal width grows, and the spectral function evolves from a narrow Breit-Wigner-like resonance peak into a transport peak, confirming the QNM prediction that the vanishing of the pole mass is accompanied by the emergence of a transport peak and making it difficult to identify a quasiparticle peak. A numerical extraction of the dispersion relation shows that the propagator can be described by a finite-temperature simple-pole form with momentum-dependent thermal width, characterized by a diffusion coefficient \(D(T)\) and an effective propagation speed \(u(T)\), whose temperature dependences are also extracted. This form modifies the usual relation between the screening and pole masses. These results may provide a useful reference for effective studies of the hot hadronic medium.
papers.reason: Uses a machine-learning-improved holographic QCD model to study thermal spectral functions and quasi-normal modes of the rho meson.

papers.title: Displaced tracks as a signal of dark matter co-annihilation: a case study using inert doublet model at $e^+e^-$ collider
papers.abstract: Dark sector containing heavy (charged) particles with small mass splitting with dark matter (DM) can co-annihilate and produce correct relic density, evading direct detection bounds. In such compressed spectra, the charged state can be long-lived and decay to DM along with a very soft charged particle, giving rise to distinctive disappearing or kink track signatures at colliders. As an example, we consider the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), where the charged scalar $H^\pm$ can be nearly degenerate with the neutral DM state ($H^0$), and produce a soft pion ($\pi^\pm$) when it decays. We investigate this signature at a future $e^+e^-$ collider, focusing on electroweak $H^+H^-$ pair production and its displaced decays. By varying the mass splitting, we explore the transition from prompt soft-particle signatures to long-lived and disappearing-track signatures. Our analysis demonstrates the potential of future lepton colliders to probe the interplay between the charged-particle lifetime, its decay probability within the tracking volume, and the production rate sensitivity to the compressed DM scenarios over a broad range of masses, allowed by cosmological constraints.
papers.reason: Explores displaced tracks and disappearing charged states from dark matter co-annihilation within the Inert Doublet Model at lepton colliders.

papers.title: Strangeness suppression, the $\phi$ meson and $\Lambda\bar\Lambda$ spin correlations from exact strangeness conservation at the quark level
papers.abstract: In small collision systems strange hadrons are suppressed, and the suppression grows with the number of strange quarks. Exact strangeness conservation in a finite volume accounts for this, but when it is imposed on hadrons it leaves the $\phi$ meson unsuppressed, contrary to observation. We impose the conservation law on the strange quarks in a causally connected cluster, before hadronization, and count separately the combinations of a strange quark with the antiquark created together with it. A pair created from the vacuum cannot form a $\phi$, a pair created from a gluon can only if it loses its color. With one function of multiplicity, the mean number of strange quarks per cluster, the model describes kaons, $\phi$, $\Xi$ and $\Omega$ in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC; the data require that about half of the same-pair combinations are excluded from the $\phi$, and reject both an unsuppressed $\phi$ and a $\phi$ built only from different pairs at about five standard deviations. The same-pair combinations are those that carry the spin correlation observed in $\Lambda\bar\Lambda$ production, whose dilution is thereby tied to the $\phi$ suppression and is predicted to decrease with multiplicity
papers.reason: Examines exact strangeness conservation at the quark level to explain suppression and spin correlations in small collision systems.

papers.title: Effects of quadratic frequency chirping and carrier-envelope phase on Schwinger pair production in polarized electric fields
papers.abstract: We investigate electron-positron pair production in spatially homogeneous, time-dependent polarized electric fields using the Dirac-Heisenberg-Wigner formalism, focusing on the effects of symmetric and asymmetric quadratic frequency chirping and the carrier-envelope phase (CEP). Our analysis reveals how these field parameters govern both the momentum-space structure and the overall yield of the produced pairs. Frequency chirping substantially reshapes the momentum distributions by modifying their interference patterns and peak occupations. The momentum distributions are particularly sensitive to weak chirping, whereas strong chirping produces pronounced oscillatory and ring-like structures across all polarization states. The total pair yield increases with chirp strength, with symmetric chirping consistently producing a higher yield than asymmetric chirping for the parameter range considered. Moreover, the sensitivity of the total number density to polarization decreases progressively with increasing chirp strength, becoming negligible in the strongly chirped regime. The CEP further modifies the momentum distributions by altering their shapes and relative peak occupations, with the extent of these changes depending on the polarization state. Our findings establish a theoretical framework for exploring external-field configurations that optimize the yield of Schwinger pair production.
papers.reason: Investigates electron-positron pair production in polarized electric fields with frequency chirping using the Dirac-Heisenberg-Wigner formalism.
